solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Undesirable trade for jam-maker?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: illicit dealing, as in drug or people smuggling
second meaning: the vehicles on the road, which cause hold-ups

explanation.surface: A wry comment that making jam is an unfortunate line of business.
explanation.walkthrough: Jam-maker suggests preserves; the jam meant is a queue of cars.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both illegal dealing in goods and the stream of vehicles that clogs roads into jams.

clue.text: Appreciative, after leaving hotel, for some fuel

indicators.note: once something has left, it is no longer there, so a letter drops out

parts.note: appreciative means grateful
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A grateful guest checks out of a hotel and fills up with petrol.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankful is the quantity a fuel tank holds, so it is an amount of fuel.

clue.text: Cricketers in a game bagging a couple of fifties

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it inside, so the game wraps around the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
rounders is a bat-and-ball game played in British schools
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, here twice

explanation.surface: Cricketers play a match in which they each score two half-centuries.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifties look like cricket scores, but they are Roman numerals slipped into 'a rounders'.
explanation.definitionFit: All-rounders are cricketers who both bat and bowl to a good standard.

clue.text: City plugging financial resource that's productive

indicators.note: a plug sits inside a hole, so the city goes inside the other word

parts.note: a fund is a pool of money
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: The City of London finances an investment that turns out to be lucrative.
explanation.definitionFit: Fecund means fertile, able to produce abundantly, so it fits productive.

clue.text: Temperate miner wanting clothing for his daughter?

parts.note: clement means mild, of weather

indicators.note: lacking its clothing means stripped of its outer letters, leaving the inside

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A mild-mannered miner has no clothes for his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: The folk song 'Oh My Darling, Clementine' is about the daughter of a miner, a forty-niner in the Californian gold rush.
explanation.definitionFit: In the American folk song, Clementine is the miner's daughter, hence the question mark on this definition by example.

clue.text: What peer has, back from old country with retro-style fashion

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the last letter of old
the United Kingdom

indicators.note: retro means looking backwards, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style

explanation.surface: Something a nobleman owns, brought home from a former nation with a vintage look.
explanation.definitionFit: A dukedom is the rank or territory held by a duke, one of the peers of the realm.

clue.text: Day you will invest a thousand in bank

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or wrap, so the second word surrounds a letter

parts.note: an old form of you
K, kilo, stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: A financial plan: on a set day, you'll put a thousand pounds into the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks financial, but it is an earth embankment.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyke is an embankment built to hold back water, so it is a bank.

clue.text: Cardinal left ship somewhere in Florida

parts.note: cardinal in its sense of chief or crucial
L is the abbreviation for left
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A senior churchman leaves a ship at some Florida port.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardinal suggests a churchman; here it is the adjective meaning key.
explanation.definitionFit: Key Largo is the largest island of the Florida Keys, so it is a place in that state.

clue.text: Report of outstanding au pair

indicators.note: a report is something spoken and heard, so the answer is a sound-alike

parts.note: outstanding can mean due and also owed or owing; said together they make the sound

explanation.surface: A reference praising an excellent live-in nanny.
explanation.walkthrough: Au pair, a live-in helper, is read as French 'at pair', a pair, which is two people.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as 'a pair', the phrase means two together, which is what a duo is.

clue.text: Spy desert rodent

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
to rat is to abandon or betray, a verb sense of desert

explanation.surface: Catch sight of a small animal that lives in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: Desert looks like a sandy adjective; it is the verb meaning abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: The mole rat is a burrowing African rodent.

clue.text: Going over part of Glinka score

indicators.note: going over suggests turning back on itself, so the letters run backwards
only a portion of the following word is used

parts.note: the second to fourth letters of the composer's name

explanation.surface: Revisiting a section of a score by the Russian composer Glinka.
explanation.walkthrough: Score looks musical, beside a composer; it is a match result.
explanation.definitionFit: A score of nil means no goals or points, so the score is zero.

clue.text: Close case of burglary, with judge stopping disrespect by low criminal

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the judge is wedged into the run of letters made by the other pieces

parts.note: cheek is impudence

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the word's letters are jumbled
the case is the outer casing, so just the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters
J is the abbreviation for judge
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tight burglary case, with the judge halting the cheek of a lowlife defendant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close case' reads as a near-run trial, but Close alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheek by jowl is an idiom for side by side, crowded closely together.

clue.text: Beginner admitting learner is to have difficulties

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so a letter goes inside the word

parts.note: a founder is the one who starts something
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A novice who takes on a trainee is bound to struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounder is to struggle clumsily, so it means to have difficulties.

clue.text: Fatter? One's cut out food here

indicators.note: something cut out is removed, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: lardier means fattier, fuller of lard
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone getting fatter is told that the snack store is out of bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' reads as 'one is': one is cut out of the longer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a cool pantry where food is stored, so food is kept here.

clue.text: Clad in jacket, a low-down participant in espionage

indicators.note: to be clad is to be dressed, so the following pieces are wrapped by the garment

parts.note: a doublet is a close-fitting Renaissance jacket
taken as written
gen is British slang for information, as is low-down

explanation.surface: A shady spy in a jacket is a bit of a lowlife.
explanation.walkthrough: Low-down looks like an adjective for a lowlife, but it is the noun meaning inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: A double agent spies for one side while pretending to spy for the other, so is a participant in espionage.

clue.text: Say more than enough after turning over of king

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the little word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
rex is Latin for king
ample means plentiful

explanation.surface: A boast that the monarch's turnover is more than adequate.
explanation.walkthrough: Say is the definition here, used as in 'say, a dozen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Say can introduce an instance, exactly as the phrase 'for instance' does.

clue.text: Advanced slowly, for the most part

indicators.note: most but not all of the word is used, so its tail goes

parts.note: lento is the musical direction for slowly

explanation.surface: Someone moved forward at a crawl, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: Advanced looks like moved forward; it means loaned, as with money.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance money is to lend it, so advanced is the past tense lent.

clue.text: With sitar periodically playing sing out forte

indicators.note: playing suggests performing freely, so the combined letters are rearranged
periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician playing the sitar now and then belts out a song loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: Forte looks like the musical direction for loud, fitting the scene; it is the noun meaning a speciality.
explanation.definitionFit: A forte is something one is especially good at, which is what a strong suit is.

clue.text: Narcissist's failing badly in a game to hold onto ball

indicators.note: holding onto something keeps it inside, so the ball goes within
done badly means done wrongly, so the letters are messed up

parts.note: taken as written
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A self-obsessed player performs poorly in a match by refusing to pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Egomania is obsessive self-regard, the flaw typical of a narcissist.

clue.text: Check energy in sweet food

parts.note: to stem a flow is to check it
ginger means vigour or pep

explanation.surface: Someone checks how much energy is in a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy in' suggests the abbreviation E going inside something; energy is a whole word here and 'in' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Stem ginger is the preserved young root of ginger in syrup, a sweet treat.

clue.text: Many fleeing country with ill-gotten gains act confidently

parts.note: swag is stolen loot

indicators.note: whatever flees is gone, so those letters are dropped from the country

parts.note: the European nation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gang running off abroad with their loot strut about boldly.
explanation.walkthrough: Many is not a crowd but the letters removed from the country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To swagger is to walk or behave with arrogant self-assurance.

clue.text: Gnome eating large salad

indicators.note: what is eaten ends up inside the eater, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: a gnome is a pithy saying, as is a saw
L is the clothing size large

explanation.surface: A garden gnome tucks into a big bowl of salad.
explanation.walkthrough: Gnome is not the garden ornament but an old word for a maxim.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaw, short for coleslaw, is a shredded cabbage salad.

clue.text: Thrilled comment about priest's riding trick

indicators.note: about means around, so the exclamation goes round the priest

parts.note: whee is a cry of delight
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: An excited remark about a clergyman's stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'priest's' reads as 'priest is', the 's joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheelie is a stunt of riding a bike on its back wheel with the front lifted.

clue.text: A little bloomer from news source without knowledge

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the paper goes round the other word

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper
lore is traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: A small gaffe by a newspaper that did not know the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomer looks like a blunder, but it is something that blooms; without means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A floret is a small flower, especially one in a cluster, so a little thing that blooms.

clue.text: Feign problem in sea, swimming

indicators.note: the problem sits within the other word
swimming suggests moving around freely, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Pretend to be in difficulty while bathing in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume a manner is to put it on falsely, as to feign it.

clue.text: Relieve pressure with everything consumed by me

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
all means everything; with just joins
consumed by me is read as I ate

explanation.surface: Easing the strain by eating the lot myself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumed by me' becomes the sentence 'I ate'.
explanation.definitionFit: To palliate is to ease symptoms without curing, so it means to relieve.

clue.text: Interpret article penned by Marx or Engels?

indicators.note: penned means shut in a pen, so the article is enclosed

parts.note: a red is a communist, as both men were
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Making sense of a piece written by one of the founders of communism.
explanation.walkthrough: Penned looks like written, but it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a situation is to interpret it, as in reading someone's mood.

clue.text: Inexperienced footballer is tender of course

parts.note: green means naive or new
the goalkeeper

explanation.surface: A rookie footballer is, naturally, a sensitive soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' reads as naturally, but course is the golf course and tender is one who tends.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenkeeper looks after a golf course, so tends it.

clue.text: Tip, either one from Eve, Norman and David

indicators.note: either end of each name serves, since each name begins and ends with the same letter

parts.note: the first, and also last, letter
the first, and also last, letter
the first, and also last, letter

explanation.surface: Advice given by a trio of named people.
explanation.walkthrough: Each name starts and ends with the same letter, so 'either one' end works.
explanation.definitionFit: The tip of something is its end or extremity.

clue.text: Evasive sort of scoundrel losing face

indicators.note: the face is the front, so losing it drops the first letter

parts.note: a heel is a cad

explanation.surface: A slippery character, a rogue who has been humiliated.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone slippery and hard to pin down is called an eel, after the wriggling fish.

clue.text: Dismiss site in Yorkshire Dales with no beers

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside town in North Yorkshire

indicators.note: having none of something means it is taken away from the word

parts.note: taken as written
ales are beers

explanation.surface: Turfed out of a pub in the Yorkshire Dales that has run dry.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yorkshire Dales, a national park, look like one phrase; Yorkshire belongs with site and Dales loses its beers.
explanation.definitionFit: To red-card a footballer is to show the red card that sends them off, so to dismiss them.

clue.text: Name of Parisian in hat drinking tea, we hear

parts.note: en is French for in

indicators.note: what is drunk goes inside the drinker, so the hat holds the next piece

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the letter is one that sounds like the word

parts.note: the letter's name is said like the drink

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's name, overheard while he sips tea in his hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle is to give a title to, so to name a book or person.
